correctness.rationale: PASS. The polar of the canonical zero-sum Lipschitz-free unit ball on m>=3 disjoint terminal-to-terminal 3-edge paths is the edge-difference <=1 potential polytope modulo constants. Polar vertices have a connected spanning saturated-edge graph, hence integral potentials. Bipartiteness forces every original edge difference odd, and therefore |difference|=1; the common three-edge path total is ±1 or ±3. For B-A=1, states (-1,0),(1,0),(1,2) give 3^m potentials; ±3 contributes only one pair, recovering the prior total 2(3^m+1) (NOT claimed novel). The centered squared normal for counts a+b+c=m is (m+1)/2+2(a+c)-2(c-a)^2/(m+1); the special ±3 squared norm is (m+9)/2. Maximizing forces b=0 and balanced a,c, giving R²=(5m+1)/2-2(m mod2)/(m+1), correct contact counts, and radius 1/R. Central symmetry makes the centered ball globally maximal, not just at origin. For all optimal centers, opposite active normals force orthogonality; their span has rank m for even m (one balanced word size) and m+1 for odd (two adjacent sizes), nonactive facets have strict slack, so affine center-set dimensions are m+1 or m. Independently enumerated all 3^m+1 positive-sign potential words and exact rational centered norms for m=3..8; all 6 maxima/contact counts and exact SymPy rational normal ranks matched. The independent finite checks cannot replace the all-m argument.
